title: Evaluating GenAI startups in cybersecurity: an analysis framework
author: Dinis Cruz
thesis: Many GenAI cybersecurity startups are solving the wrong problem, or solving the right problem in a way that doesn't survive the next model improvement.

criteria.name: Structural vs. Temporary
criteria.heading: Are you solving a structural problem or a temporary mess?
criteria.question: If every enterprise had perfect visibility and control over their AI deployments tomorrow, would this company still have a product?
criteria.red: Solving symptoms of current GenAI mess
criteria.green: Solving fundamental enterprise problems that persist as AI matures

criteria.name: Unit Value
criteria.heading: Can you deliver value without mass adoption?
criteria.question: Can this product deliver value on a single use case, for a single team, on day one?
criteria.red: Requires enterprise-wide deployment for any value
criteria.green: Delivers value to a single team on day one

criteria.name: Inline Risk
criteria.heading: What happens when you go inline?
criteria.question: Is this product designed to be inline (intercepting, filtering, modifying LLM traffic)? If so, how do they handle false positives, latency, context-dependent decisions, and the inevitable blame when something goes wrong?
criteria.red: Product is inline with LLM traffic, single point of failure
criteria.green: Out-of-band, non-blocking, or inline with robust context handling

criteria.name: Business Context
criteria.heading: How are you modelling business context?
criteria.question: How do you handle a situation where the same prompt is dangerous in Department A but legitimate in Department B?
criteria.red: LLM analysing LLM output, no business model
criteria.green: Semantic graphs, permission models, workflow-aware decisions

criteria.name: Model Survivability
criteria.heading: When the next model ships, do you get better or gain a competitor?
criteria.question: When the next generation of models arrives, does this company get better, or gain a competitor?
criteria.red: Value disappears when next model ships

criteria.name: Open Source
criteria.heading: Is the open source strategy real or lock-in?
criteria.question: Can a motivated team take the open source project and, without purchasing anything, solve a real problem end-to-end?
criteria.red: Lock-in open source, can't solve real problem without paying
criteria.green: Genuinely open core, moat is execution not code

criteria.name: Deployment Sovereignty
criteria.heading: Can you deploy everywhere, in complete isolation?
criteria.question: Can this product be deployed in a completely air-gapped environment with zero communication to any external service?

criteria.name: Architecture
criteria.heading: Agentic architecture vs. LLMs inline
criteria.question: Is the business operating in an agentic way, with AI helping humans write better code, build better rules, and understand business context, or is the AI an inline execution engine?

bands.label: Rare
bands.meaning: structurally strong company with durable advantages

not_evaluated: Team quality, which matters enormously but requires different evaluation methods
Current traction, since a company can have great traction in a temporary market
Financial metrics: revenue, burn rate and unit economics matter but are orthogonal to these criteria
Specific technical capabilities, as the framework is deliberately technology-agnostic
Go-to-market execution, since a structurally strong company can still fail on execution
